solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Female is drunk, engaging another female in tussle

indicators.note: engaging here means holding or taking in, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk
a second F, the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A drunken woman gets into a scrap with another woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaging' signals a container: the second female goes inside the word for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A fistfight is a brawl with bare hands, a kind of physical scuffle.

clue.text: Admit being kept under by father displaying severe expression

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece kept under another is written below it, so it comes second

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
to own is to admit or confess

explanation.surface: Someone forced to confess under a father's thumb looks stern.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'being kept under by' means written below, so the father comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A frown is the knitted-brow look that conveys displeasure or sternness.

clue.text: Item in first-aid kit: splint, say, and gear with splint, possibly

parts.note: a splint is a thin strip of wood, an example of a stick

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A first-aid kit inventory: a splint, plus some equipment to go with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges GEAR and SPLINT into INGPLASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticking plaster is an adhesive dressing for small cuts, a staple of any first-aid box.

clue.text: Location in Europe's fine planetary vehicles?

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
landers are spacecraft that touch down on a planet's surface

explanation.surface: A question about where Europe's excellent planetary probes might be found.
explanation.walkthrough: FLANDERS is a region of northern Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Flanders is a historic region straddling Belgium, France and the Netherlands, so a place on that continent.

clue.text: £1000 getting a lot of rubbish wine

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds

indicators.note: a lot of, but not all, means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: crud is slang for rubbish or filth

explanation.surface: Paying a thousand pounds for plonk that is largely rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops the last letter of CRUD to leave CRU.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand cru is the top classification of French vineyard, applied to its finest bottles.

clue.text: Critical comment about origins of Manchester United likely to produce uproar

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: tut is an exclamation of disapproval

indicators.note: origins are beginnings, so each word gives its first letter

explanation.surface: Criticism of Manchester United's roots is bound to cause a furore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origins of' takes M, U and L from Manchester, United and likely; 'about' puts TUT around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumult is loud confused commotion, the same din as an uproar.

clue.text: More than one picket comments on website

definitions.meaning: messages put up on an online forum

explanation.surface: A striker's picket line chatter appears online.
explanation.definitionFit: Posts are both upright stakes like pickets and entries contributed to a web page.

clue.text: Particular person in prison will be visited by US lawyer

indicators.note: being visited by means having someone come inside, so one piece enters the other

parts.note: pent means penned or shut in, as a prisoner is
a DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: A certain inmate is due a visit from an American attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Particular' is the fussy sense, not 'specific'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant is a fussy stickler for detail, someone particular in that sense.

clue.text: One ascending by twisted means will aggravate a satirical press

indicators.note: to aggravate is to stir up and disturb, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A climber's devious methods will rile a mocking newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will aggravate' rearranges A SATIRICAL PRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiral staircase winds round a central column, so whoever climbs it goes up by a twisting route.

clue.text: Computer programs to do some running battle in London area

indicators.note: in places these pieces within the other

parts.note: SE is the South East London postcode district
to hare is to run fast
war is a battle on a large scale

explanation.surface: A race and a fight taking place in a part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; London's postal districts are named by compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Shareware is software distributed free to try, with payment asked for continued use.

clue.text: Love family vacationing perhaps in Scotland or Japanese city

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
kin are one's relatives
awa is the Scots form of away, as someone on holiday is

explanation.surface: A sweetheart's relatives holidaying in Scotland or in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: AWA is the Scottish spelling of away.
explanation.definitionFit: Okinawa is the chief town of the southern Japanese island group of the same name.

clue.text: Produced a lot of revolutionary dry wine

parts.note: made means produced

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning round, so these letters are read backwards
a lot of, but not all, means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: arid means dry

explanation.surface: Someone produced a large batch of dry wine with radical flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' cuts ARID to ARI and 'revolutionary' turns it to IRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a fortified wine from the Portuguese Atlantic island of that name.

clue.text: Moved twistily, heading off out of cover

indicators.note: the heading is the first letter, which goes off, leaving the rest

parts.note: snaked means wound along like a snake

explanation.surface: Someone weaved away, heading out of shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes S from SNAKED.
explanation.definitionFit: Naked means uncovered, with no clothing or protection over it.

clue.text: Trace European policy in time

indicators.note: in places these pieces within the other

parts.note: a date is a point in time
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: Tracking a European policy over a period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal: the European policy sits within the time.
explanation.definitionFit: To delineate is to draw the outline of something, as tracing does.

clue.text: Awkward study with a run bagged in Test

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: something bagged in a container is held inside it

parts.note: try means test, as in try it out
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A cricketer's tricky analysis of a run scored in a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bagged in' puts A and R inside TRY. A Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrary means perverse or obstinate, which is how an awkward person behaves.

clue.text: Extensive international lying not admitting of remedy

parts.note: a cap is a player chosen for their country, named after the cap awarded

indicators.note: not admitting means keeping out, so these letters are left out

parts.note: mendacious means untruthful
to mend is to remedy or fix

explanation.surface: A sweeping charge that a national player is lying beyond cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not admitting of' removes MEND from MENDACIOUS, leaving ACIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Capacious means roomy and able to hold a great deal, so vast or wide-ranging.

clue.text: Part of the world, mostly unchanged area

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: as is means in the present state, without changes

explanation.surface: A region of the globe, largely left just as it was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims AS IS to ASI.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest continent, one of the major divisions of the globe.

clue.text: Squeeze garden into trimmed surroundings

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: shorn means trimmed, and these letters form the surroundings for the other piece
to hoe is to work the garden soil

explanation.surface: Cramming a garden plot into a neatly clipped setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals the container; 'trimmed surroundings' says the word for trimmed is the outer part.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoehorn is to force something into a tight space, as a shoe-horn eases a foot in.

clue.text: Is this a pen-supplier? Answer (Y/N) after review

indicators.note: review suggests reworking, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters Y and N, as on a yes-or-no form

explanation.surface: A quiz asking whether this is where to get a pen, with a yes/no box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after review' rearranges ANSWER plus Y and N. A pen is a female swan, not a writing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A swannery is a place where swans are bred, so it supplies pens, the female birds.

clue.text: Tubing that is partly interfering with pianos?

indicators.note: only part of the abbreviation, its first letter, interferes by coming between the two P's

parts.note: p is the music abbreviation for piano (softly), so two pianos are PP
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Plumbing that gets in the way of the pianos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly interfering with' moves only the I of IE between the two P's, leaving E at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe is a length of tube, so tubing in the general sense.

clue.text: Footwear placed outside toilet when giving display

indicators.note: a piece placed outside another surrounds it

parts.note: a shoe is an item of footwear
WC is water closet, a toilet
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A shoe left outside the loo while putting on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placed outside' signals the container: the footwear wraps round the toilet and 'when'.
explanation.definitionFit: A showcase is a setting in which things are shown off, a display.

clue.text: Travelling overseas? There's romance about the unknown

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a fling is a brief love affair
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A holiday romance with a mysterious stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts FLING around Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying is one way of travelling abroad, by air over the sea; the question mark flags an example.

clue.text: Articles on source of music, church music?

parts.note: an and the are the articles of English grammar

indicators.note: the source is the beginning, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Pieces written about where church music comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' gives M from music.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a choral composition sung in church services, one example of church music.

clue.text: Take on chief leading all-English league at last

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A leading figure eventually heads an all-English sports league.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' takes E from league.
explanation.definitionFit: To challenge is to confront or compete against, which is what taking someone on means.

clue.text: No remorse, ditching University bridge player

indicators.note: ditching means getting rid of, so a letter is removed

parts.note: ruth is an old word for pity or remorse, as in ruthless

explanation.surface: A student quits university without a shred of regret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditching' removes U from RUTH, leaving RTH.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the four players are named by compass points, so North is one seat.

clue.text: Composer's vacation close to forest

parts.note: hols is British slang for holidays

indicators.note: the close is the end, so the final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A musician's holiday cottage near the woods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' gives T from forest. HOLS is the everyday British short form of holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Holst was the English composer of The Planets suite.

clue.text: No flights for me? East of Germany well-supplied

parts.note: Ost is German for east
rich means abundantly provided

explanation.surface: A traveller in well-off eastern Germany refuses to fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East of Germany' means east in German, not Germany's eastern region.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is a bird that cannot fly, so it would never take flights itself.

clue.text: Omnipotent in general

definitions.meaning: one who is ... holds power above everything

explanation.surface: A short phrase about an all-powerful being in general terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Overall means generally, and read as over all it describes supreme power.

clue.text: Silence covering revelation of resignation

parts.note: sh is a call for silence
a rug is a floor covering

explanation.surface: Keeping quiet about a disclosure that someone has quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resignation' means acceptance, not quitting a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrug of the shoulders shows that one is resigned to something one cannot change.

clue.text: Ready-to-wear accessory?

parts.note: ready is slang for cash, so this is an accessory worn for carrying money, not a fashion item

explanation.surface: A fashion item sold off the peg.
explanation.walkthrough: Ready is slang for cash, as in ready money.
explanation.definitionFit: A money belt is worn round the waist to hold cash, an accessory for wearing one's ready money.
